title: Say No to Food Waste on Campus
prompt: Write an essay on food waste on campus. You should include: 1) the phenomenon; 2) the reasons; 3) your suggestions.
outline: 现象：食堂剩饭剩菜普遍
原因：点太多 / 口味不合 / 缺乏意识
建议：按需取餐、小份菜、宣传与监督
sample:
Food waste has become a common sight on campus. Every day, large amounts of rice and vegetables are thrown away in the dining hall.

The reasons are not hard to find. Some students order more than they can eat, some dislike the taste, and many simply do not realize how serious the problem is. What they forget is that every bowl of rice costs water, land and labour.

To change this, canteens can offer smaller portions at lower prices, and students should take only what they need. Posters and volunteer checks may also help. Waste is a habit, and habits can be replaced.

title: Do Smartphones Help or Harm Our Study?
prompt: Some say smartphones are useful learning tools; others say they distract students. Write an essay stating your view with examples.
outline: 双面性：查资料/背单词 vs 短视频/消息
关键是自控力与方法
结论：工具中性，取决于使用方式
sample:
The smartphone is a double-edged sword for students. On one hand, it puts a dictionary, a vocabulary app and a library in our pocket. On the other hand, a short video can swallow an entire evening.

In my experience, the difference lies not in the phone but in the user. When I set a timer and put the phone face down, it becomes a tool. When I hold it "just to check a message", it becomes a trap.

Therefore, we should not blame the device. We should learn to control the way we use it, because in the long run self-control matters more than any app.

title: Should College Students Take Part-time Jobs?
prompt: Write an essay on whether college students should take part-time jobs. Give your reasons.
outline: 支持：接触社会、赚生活费、练沟通
反对：耽误学业、被廉价劳动消耗
我的观点：有选择地做，优先与专业相关
sample:
Whether students should take part-time jobs has long been debated. Supporters say such jobs offer working experience and pocket money; critics warn that they may take time away from study.

Both sides have a point. A job in a cafe teaches communication, but carrying plates for ten hours a week at the cost of sleep is not education. The key is to strike a balance.

In my view, students should choose jobs that are related to their major or that develop a skill they lack. A part-time job is a supplement to study, never a substitute for it.

title: How Students Read: Paper or Screen?
prompt: The chart shows how students in one university read between 2020 and 2025: paper reading fell from 70% to 35%, while screen reading rose from 30% to 65%. Describe the trend and give your comments.
outline: 描述趋势：纸质下降、电子上升、2022 年前后交叉
原因：手机普及、电子书便宜、碎片时间
评论：便利但伤眼、深度阅读仍需纸质
sample:
The chart reveals a clear shift in the way students read. In 2020, paper reading accounted for 70% and screen reading only 30%. By 2025, the figures had almost reversed, with screen reading rising to 65%.

Several factors explain the trend. Smartphones make texts available anywhere, e-books are cheaper, and fragmented time is easier to fill with a screen. In contrast, paper books require a desk and a quiet hour.

Convenience, however, is not the whole story. Screens tire the eyes and encourage skimming. For serious reading, I still believe paper deserves a place.

title: An Email to Your Foreign Teacher
prompt: Write an email to your foreign teacher, Mr. Smith, asking to join the English Corner and explaining what you can offer.
outline: 称呼与来意
自我介绍 + 想加入的原因
能贡献什么（组织/摄影/话题）
期待回复 + 落款
sample:
Dear Mr. Smith,

I am writing to ask whether I could join the English Corner this term. I am a second-year student and I would like to practise speaking in a real conversation rather than in front of a mirror.

I am willing to help with organization: I can design topics, take photos, and arrive early to set up the room. Last year I helped run a reading club, so I know how to keep a discussion going.

I look forward to your reply.

Yours sincerely,
Li Ming

title: Will AI Take Away Our Jobs?
prompt: Write an essay on whether artificial intelligence will take away human jobs. State your opinion with reasons.
outline: 担忧：重复性工作被替代
反驳：历史上技术也创造新岗位
真正的问题：转型期的错配与再培训
结论：与其恐惧，不如学习
sample:
The rise of artificial intelligence has raised a familiar fear: machines will take our jobs. The fear is understandable, since AI already writes, translates and answers questions.

History, however, suggests a more complicated story. Technology removes some tasks but creates new positions, and the people who adapt usually do better than those who wait. The real problem is not the total number of jobs but the mismatch during the transition.

Therefore, the answer is not to slow down technology but to learn faster. In a changing job market, the safest skill is the ability to learn.

title: Should Phones Be Banned in Class?
prompt: Some teachers ask students to hand in their phones before class. Others say phones are useful learning tools. What is your opinion? Write an essay of 120-180 words.
outline: 表明立场：有限度地管，而不是一刀切禁止
理由一：课堂上手机最大的问题是注意力，不是手机本身
理由二：查词、记录、随堂检索确实有用，该留口子
结论：规则要清楚，执行要一致
sample:
Some schools now collect students' phones before class. In my view, a clear rule is better than a total ban, and a total ban is better than no rule at all.

The real problem with phones in class is not the phone but the attention it steals. A single message can pull a student out of a forty-minute lecture, and it takes several minutes to get back. Teachers are therefore right to ask for phones to be put away during explanations and discussions.

However, phones are also useful tools. Students look up new words, record the teacher's key points and check facts in a second. If phones are banned completely, these small advantages disappear as well. A workable rule is simple: phones stay in bags during lectures and come out only when the teacher asks for them.

Rules work when everyone follows the same ones. A clear, consistent policy protects attention without throwing away a useful tool.

title: How College Students Spend Their Free Time
prompt: The chart shows how 500 students in one university spend their free time: short videos 38%, sports 21%, reading 17%, part-time jobs 14%, other 10%. Describe the chart and give your comment.
outline: 第一段：描述图表，点出最大项和第二项
第二段：分析原因（短视频门槛低、运动需要场地和时间）
第三段：给建议，落到可执行的一步
sample:
The chart shows how 500 students at one university spend their free time. Short videos account for the largest proportion, at 38%, followed by sports at 21% and reading at 17%. Part-time jobs take 14%, and the remaining 10% goes to other activities.

Two points stand out. First, short videos are cheap to start: no equipment, no partner, no fixed time. A student can open an app in the queue for lunch. Sports, by contrast, need a court, a partner and a free hour, which explains why they come second. Reading sits in the middle, probably because it requires quiet and a settled mind.

The imbalance is worth noticing. Thirty-eight percent of free time is a lot to give to something that leaves almost nothing behind. A simple fix is to decide the night before what the next day's free hour is for, and to keep the phone out of reach while doing it.

title: An Email About Sharing Housework
zh: 给室友写邮件商量分担家务
prompt: Your roommate never does the cleaning. Write an email of 100-150 words to him or her: describe the problem, suggest a fair way to share the work, and keep the tone friendly.
outline: 先客气开场，说明不是抱怨
具体说清问题（垃圾、地面、洗碗）
提出可执行的轮值方案
留出商量余地
useful: let me know what you think
sample:
Hi Sam,

I'm writing about something small but repeated: the cleaning. I'm not complaining about you, but the rubbish, the floor and the dishes have mostly been on my side for the past three weeks, and it is starting to wear me out.

Could we take turns? A simple schedule might work: I do the rubbish and the floor on Monday and Thursday, you do them on Tuesday and Friday, and we both wash our own dishes the same evening. Weekends we can do together in twenty minutes.

If the days don't suit you, tell me which ones do. I'd rather agree on a plan than keep guessing.

Thanks,
Li Ming

title: Can Online Courses Replace the Classroom?
prompt: Online courses are cheap and flexible, yet many students still prefer sitting in a classroom. Write an essay of 120-180 words giving your view.
outline: 立场：能替代一部分，不能替代全部
网课的优势：可回看、可暂停、跨地域
课堂不可替代的地方：节奏、提问、同伴压力
结论：混合使用，而不是二选一
sample:
Online courses have made good teaching cheap and portable. A student in a small town can now watch the same lecture as one in a big city. But cheap access is not the same as a complete education, and online courses cannot replace the classroom entirely.

The strengths of online learning are real. Videos can be paused and replayed, which suits students who need a second pass at a difficult point. Materials can be updated in a day instead of a semester.

The classroom offers something different: a shared pace and a shared audience. When a teacher asks a question, everyone in the room feels the same small pressure to think. That pressure is hard to reproduce through a screen, and it is often what turns listening into learning.

The sensible answer is not to choose sides. Use online courses for what they do best, such as reviewing and drilling, and keep the classroom for discussion, questions and the discipline of showing up.
